evidence.observation: Computes 3 × 3 = 9 Inventory calls per original request and up to 1,800 attempts/s from 200 requests/s. Presents this as a potential amplified load/steady-state implication under the stated timeout assumptions, distinguishes additional client retries and unknown overlap, and does not claim measured sustained throughput.

Proposes one Checkout and one Inventory attempt, a 1.8-second ingress deadline with propagated remaining budget, 100 ms acquisition and a one-second full Inventory-call cap. Accounts for ongoing downstream work after caller expiry: retain connection/capacity ownership until actual completion or confirmed abort; five-second supervisor escalation does not permit unsafe reuse.

Removes timeout retry amplification for the read-only availability path, caps concurrency against measured healthy capacity, rejects excess work rather than allowing an unbounded queue, and retains accounting for unfinished work. Removing retries plus bounded admission is a justified alternative overload-control mechanism; backoff/jitter is not needed on a removed retry path.

Proposes 200 requests/s with one-second Inventory timeouts and explicit limits: at most 200 Inventory dispatches/s, responses within two seconds, active calls below the configured cap and queue wait at most 100 ms. Measures cancellation completion and temporary unavailability, restores Inventory and checks useful work/retry-surge/stranded-work recovery. No circuit-breaker recovery guarantee is claimed.
